structured.approach:
I followed DS-07 in the data-science-steps skill and read all three contracted inputs: task.code, task.unit_tests and feat.stories. The step hook blocks every shell command, so I ran no git command and no CI. Instead I read the ap_forecast checkout's git metadata (.git/config, refs/heads/main, dev and feature/story, packed-refs, logs/HEAD, the feature/story reflog and COMMIT_EDITMSG) and the changed source files. I used Glob to look for merge state and Grep to look for conflict markers and secrets, and memory_search to check the commit convention. I also read the previous attempt's draft of task.commit and the CI result the spine recorded on it.

What I found: the spine has already committed the tree as 9eff98d and CI passed on it. The commit message is 'STORY # task.commit: FEAT-ZD-48600', which breaks the rule that commit messages start with the story ID. The commit has not been pushed.

I rewrote task.commit in full. It records the real repository state, the 7 files and which story each serves, the CI result, the fast-forward push to origin feature/story, and the traced commit message to use. Changing only the message of an unpushed commit keeps the tree that passed CI. Whether to reword before the push is a decision for the Developer, so I raised it as BLOCKING question DSQ-4. I also corrected the task.unit_tests revision to 3777aa5.
